newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up, boosted by foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up, boosted by foreign demand.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index firmed 0.38 percent on Tuesday as foreign investors flirted with the market but traders forecast little change over the next two weeks due to the summer holidays.

"Stronger foreign demand brought fresh optimism and pulled prices up but that will not be enough for continuous growth," one trader said. "Demand is not likely to remain strong this week due to the holidays."
"I expect shares will oscillate slightly by up to half a percent daily either way throughout the next two weeks," he added.
* The SBI index firmed 5.83 points, or 0.38 percent, to 1,540.67.
* Drug maker Lek was most actively traded, up 0.99 percent to 35,600 tolars on volume of 8,537 shares.
